canh-khoai-mon-chay-dau-hu.name: Vegetarian Taro and Tofu Soup
canh-khoai-mon-chay-dau-hu.serving_basis: A pot of soup for four to share with rice.
canh-khoai-mon-chay-dau-hu.description: Taro simmers with tofu and leek in a gently seasoned vegetarian broth. Serve this hot soup as part of a Vietnamese family vegetarian meal.
canh-khoai-mon-chay-dau-hu.finished_dish: The taro is tender and lightly fluffy while holding its shape; the tofu is seasoned through, and the broth is mild with fragrant leek and herbs.
canh-khoai-mon-chay-dau-hu.serving: Serve hot with rice, black pepper, rice paddy herb, and culantro.
tips: Wear gloves when peeling taro to reduce skin irritation.
Add vegetarian fish sauce gradually because salt levels vary by brand.
Add the herbs at the end to preserve their aroma.

canh-khoai-mon-chay-dau-hu.media_alt_text: A bowl of vegetarian taro and tofu soup with clear broth, rice paddy herb, and culantro.
canh-khoai-mon-chay-dau-hu.time_note: About 55 minutes; timing varies with the size of the taro pieces and heat level.

preparation_steps: Rinse the soil from the taro, boil it with a little salt for 5–7 minutes, cool, then peel and cut into bite-size pieces.
Drain and cube the tofu. Mince the leek; rinse and chop the rice paddy herb and culantro.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the leek until fragrant. Add the tofu and gently stir until lightly firm and aromatic.
Bring the water to a boil, add the tofu, then add the taro. Season with some of the vegetarian seasoning, vegetarian fish sauce, and sugar.
Simmer over medium heat until the taro is tender, about 15–20 minutes if parboiled. Adjust the seasoning, add pepper and herbs, and turn off the heat.

mang-xao-nam-bao-ngu.name: Stir-Fried Bamboo Shoots with Oyster Mushrooms
aliases: Vegetarian Bamboo Shoot and Oyster Mushroom Stir-Fry
mang-xao-nam-bao-ngu.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for four people.
mang-xao-nam-bao-ngu.description: Fresh bamboo shoots are stir-fried with oyster mushrooms, leek, and celery. Use plant-based vegetarian oyster sauce to keep the dish meat-free, and serve with rice.
mang-xao-nam-bao-ngu.finished_dish: The bamboo shoots are tender without a raw edge; the oyster mushrooms are soft and savory, with seasoning evenly coating the vegetables.
mang-xao-nam-bao-ngu.serving: Serve hot with rice and a small dish of soy sauce with chili if desired.
tips: Boil fresh bamboo shoots thoroughly and change the water before stir-frying.
Drain the mushrooms well to avoid excess liquid in the pan.

mang-xao-nam-bao-ngu.time_note: About 45 minutes, including preparation and boiling the fresh bamboo shoots.

preparation_steps: Rinse and slice the bamboo shoots. Boil uncovered, changing the cooking water a few times to remove bitterness, then drain.
Trim the oyster mushrooms and tear them into bite-size pieces. Rinse and cut the celery; finely chop the leek.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the leek for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the bamboo shoots and mushrooms, then season with soy sauce, vegetarian oyster sauce, sugar, and vegetarian seasoning powder. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes.
Add about 100 ml water and bring to a boil until the ingredients are tender. Stir in the celery and turn off the heat.

dau-bap-xao-nam-chay.name: Vegetarian Okra and Oyster Mushroom Stir-Fry
dau-bap-xao-nam-chay.serving_basis: A quick vegetable side dish for two.
dau-bap-xao-nam-chay.description: Green okra is quickly stir-fried with oyster mushrooms, garlic, and scallions. It is a simple vegetable dish for a light everyday vegetarian meal.
dau-bap-xao-nam-chay.finished_dish: The okra is just tender with some crunch; the mushrooms are soft and savory, with fragrant garlic and lightly balanced seasoning.
dau-bap-xao-nam-chay.serving: Serve immediately with rice; add soy sauce at the table if a deeper flavor is wanted.
tips: Choose young, medium-sized okra for a tender texture.
Drain the mushrooms before adding them to the pan.
Stir-fry the okra briefly over high heat to preserve its green color and crispness.

Mince the white part and cut the greens.
preparation_steps: Trim the okra, rinse and drain it, then cut diagonally into pieces about 1–2 cm thick.
Trim the oyster mushrooms, briefly rinse in lightly salted water, rinse again and drain well. Mince the garlic and slice the scallions.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil over medium-low heat and sauté the garlic with the white part of the scallions until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry for about 1 minute. Increase the heat, add the okra, sugar, salt, and optional MSG.
Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until the okra is just tender. Adjust the seasoning, add scallion greens and pepper, then turn off the heat.

canh-bi-dao-nhoi-chay.name: Vegetarian Stuffed Winter Melon Soup
aliases: Winter Melon Stuffed with Tofu and Mushrooms
canh-bi-dao-nhoi-chay.serving_basis: A pot of soup for four to share with rice.
canh-bi-dao-nhoi-chay.description: Winter melon rings are filled with tofu, mushrooms, and vegetarian protein, then simmered with straw mushrooms. The clear soup has a mild, savory broth for a home-style vegetarian meal.
canh-bi-dao-nhoi-chay.finished_dish: The melon rings hold their shape and the tofu-mushroom filling is cooked through; the broth is light and fragrant with straw mushrooms and cilantro.
canh-bi-dao-nhoi-chay.serving: Serve each bowl with a few stuffed melon rings, broth, and straw mushrooms while hot.
tips: Cut the melon thick enough to hold the filling.
Drain the mushrooms well so the filling does not become watery.
Dust the top of the filling lightly with cornstarch to help it stay in place.

preparation_steps: Peel the melon, cut it into 3–4 cm rings, and scoop out the centers. Soak in lightly salted water for 5–10 minutes, rinse, and drain.
Soak the vegetarian mock ribs until soft, drain, and mince. Prepare the oyster and straw mushrooms; mince the mushrooms used in the filling.
Mix the tofu, oyster mushrooms, and mock ribs with some vegetarian seasoning and pepper. Add the wood ear mushrooms and combine.
cooking_steps: Fill the melon rings with the mixture and press gently. Dust the top of the filling with a thin layer of cornstarch.
Heat the oil and stir-fry the straw mushrooms for about 2 minutes. Add the water, salt, and some vegetarian seasoning; bring to a boil.
Add the stuffed melon rings, lower the heat, and simmer until the melon and filling are cooked, about 20–25 minutes. Adjust the broth, garnish with cilantro and optional chili powder.

dau-hu-hap-nam-chay.name: Steamed Tofu with Mushrooms
aliases: Vegetarian Steamed Tofu with Straw Mushrooms
dau-hu-hap-nam-chay.serving_basis: A light tofu dish for two people.
dau-hu-hap-nam-chay.description: Soft tofu is steamed and topped with straw mushrooms sautéed with leek, vegetarian oyster sauce, and soy sauce. It is an easy, mild dish to add to a Vietnamese vegetarian meal.
dau-hu-hap-nam-chay.finished_dish: The tofu stays soft and warm; the straw mushrooms are seasoned through with a light savory-sweet sauce.
dau-hu-hap-nam-chay.serving: Finish with scallions and optional chili; serve hot with rice.
tips: Place the tofu on a heatproof plate before steaming to avoid breaking it during transfer.
Cook the mushroom topping before pouring it over the tofu.
Omit chili sauce and fresh chili for a mild version.

preparation_steps: Trim the straw mushrooms, rinse briefly with lightly salted water, rinse again and drain. Cut the soft tofu into bite-size cubes.
Mince the white part of the scallions, chop the greens, and slice the chili if using.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the scallion whites. Add the straw mushrooms, vegetarian oyster sauce, soy sauce, optional chili sauce, sugar, and optional MSG. Stir-fry for about 5 minutes until seasoned.
Arrange the tofu on a heatproof plate and steam for about 5 minutes. Spoon the mushrooms and sauce over it, then steam for another 2 minutes.
Carefully remove the plate, garnish with scallion greens and optional chili, and serve hot.
